terms.definition: The share of input energy that becomes useful output.
terms.function: Rates machines, bulbs, and engines on how little they waste.
terms.whereItIs: The percent badge above the engine's bars.
terms.whyItMatters: The lever behind fuel bills, battery life, and greener machines.

terms.definition: The percent recipe that measures the useful share of any energy conversion.
terms.whyItMatters: One formula lets you compare an LED and a filament, a car and a train.
terms.whereItIs: The number the badge computes from the two bars.

terms.definition: The input that escapes as heat, noise, or drag instead of doing useful work.
terms.whyItMatters: They are why efficiency never reaches 100% and why 'wasted' energy still exists.

terms.definition: The unavoidable rule that every real machine loses something.
terms.whyItMatters: It drives engineers to cut friction — the cheapest path to more useful output.
terms.whereItIs: The badge that always sits under the 100 line.
